findings.source_quote: Systematic reviews and meta-analyses examining stenting versus no stenting after uncomplicated ureteroscopy/ureteroscopic lithotripsy indicate that routine postoperative stenting does not necessarily improve key effectiveness outcomes (e.g., stone-free results) in uncomplicated cases, while stent-related symptoms remain a relevant burden
findings.explanation: Art.61.11 requires clinical evaluation to be updated with post-market surveillance data for class III devices and implantable devices at least annually. The CER section describes current literature but does not indicate any plan for updating the clinical evaluation with post-market surveillance data, which is a critical requirement for class III devices.
findings.suggested_correction: The clinical evaluation shall be updated at least annually with post-market surveillance data obtained from the manufacturer's PMCF plan for class III devices and implantable devices, as required by Art.61.11.

raw.violating_statement: The CER section does not provide a consideration of currently available alternative treatment options for the intended purpose of the device, as required by Art.61.3.c
raw.source_quote: The following table provides a comparison of the Double J Stent (Short Term) with alternative treatment options available for the management of ureteral obstruction and impaired urinary drainage.
raw.explanation: The clause requires a consideration of currently available alternative treatment options for the intended purpose. The CER section mentions comparing with alternative options but does not explicitly state that it has considered these options for the intended purpose of the device.
raw.suggested_correction: The section should explicitly state that it has considered currently available alternative treatment options for the intended purpose of the device, including their clinical benefits and risks.

findings.violating_statement: The statement claims no clinical investigation was performed for an implantable device, but MDR Article 61.4 requires clinical investigations for implantable devices unless specific conditions are met.
findings.source_quote: The Double J Stent/Kit (Short Term) is an implantable as it is inserted into the body for several days or weeks and then removed, this technology has indeed been in routine clinical use for over a decade. Hence, according to MDR article 61, no clinical investigation was performed.
findings.explanation: The CER section claims no clinical investigation was performed for an implantable device, but Article 61.4 states that clinical investigations shall be performed for implantable devices and class III devices unless specific conditions are met (e.g., modifications of a marketed device with equivalent demonstration). The statement does not address whether the conditions for exemption apply, thus it incorrectly concludes no clinical investigation was performed.
findings.suggested_correction: The Double J Stent/Kit (Short Term) is an implantable device that has been in routine clinical use for over a decade. Clinical investigations may not be required if the device meets the conditions specified in Article 61.4, such as being a modification of a marketed device with equivalent demonstration.

findings.violating_statement: The CER section does not include a PMCF plan as required for class IIa, IIb, or III devices under MDR
findings.source_quote: The device is marketed in India. The following data sources were utilised to collect relevant post-marketing data to support clinical safety and performance.
findings.explanation: Annex III.b requires a PMCF plan or justification for why it is not applicable. The CER section mentions post-market surveillance data but does not specify if a PMCF plan is in place or justified.
findings.suggested_correction: Include a statement that a PMCF plan is in place or provide a justification for why a PMCF plan is not applicable.

findings.violating_statement: The CER section does not provide sufficient detail on the methods and protocols to assess post-market surveillance data as required by MDR

findings.explanation: Annex III.b requires effective and appropriate methods and processes to assess the collected data. The CER section does not detail how the data was assessed.
findings.suggested_correction: Describe the methods and protocols used to assess the post-market surveillance data.

findings.violating_statement: The CER section does not include a periodic safety update report (PSUR) as required for class IIa, IIb, or III devices under MDR
